name: Start a fire with flint and steel
blurb: The traditional pre-match method: a hard stone edge shaves burning particles off high-carbon steel into char cloth. Far easier than friction fire and beautifully reliable once the char is right.
gear: A sharp-edged flint, chert, quartz or agate
Char cloth (make your own from 100% cotton in a tin)
A tinder bundle: jute, dry grass, birch bark
steps: Make char cloth: pack cotton scraps in a tin with a pinhole, put it in a fire until the smoke from the hole stops, then let it cool sealed.
Hold a piece of char cloth on top of the flint, just back from the sharp edge, pinched under your thumb.
Strike the steel down along the flint edge at a shallow angle so sparks fall onto the char, not away from it.
When a spark catches, an orange glow will spread across the char. Do not blow yet.
Fold the glowing char into your tinder bundle, close it loosely, and blow steadily until it bursts into flame.
Practise until you can do it in under a minute with cold hands.
tips: Bad char cloth is the usual culprit: if it is brown rather than uniformly black, it was under-cooked.
The flint must be sharp. Knap a fresh edge when strikes stop throwing sparks.
The steel must be high carbon. Stainless will not spark.
proof: Spark to flame in under a minute, using char cloth you made yourself.
